mean: wishing you prosperity (a New Year greeting)
lit: respectful congratulations, and may you make a fortune

use.how: Said on its own as a greeting, mostly at Spring Festival: 新年好，恭喜发财！ It wishes the listener wealth in the coming year.

near.diff: 万事如意 wishes that everything goes well and suits any occasion; 恭喜发财 wishes wealth and belongs mainly to the Lunar New Year.

cue: On the first morning of the Lunar New Year, a child greets an uncle, hoping a red envelope will follow. What does the child say?

ctx.s: 大年初一，孩子们见到爷爷就说：“{恭喜发财}！”
ctx.en: On New Year's Day the children greet their grandfather: "Happy New Year, may you prosper!"

ctx.s: 春节一大早，邻居们在楼道里互相拱手：“新年好，{恭喜发财}！”
ctx.en: Early on New Year's morning, the neighbours salute each other in the stairwell: "Happy New Year, wishing you prosperity!"

ctx.s: “{恭喜发财}，红包拿来！”小侄子笑着向我伸出手。
ctx.en: "Happy New Year, now hand over the red envelope!" my little nephew said, holding out his hand with a grin.

ctx.s: 除夕晚上老板在群里发了红包，大家纷纷回复“{恭喜发财}”。
ctx.en: On New Year's Eve the boss sent red envelopes in the group chat, and everyone replied with New Year wishes of prosperity.

ctx.s: 春节期间，饭店门口的服务员见了客人就说“{恭喜发财}”。
ctx.en: During Spring Festival, the staff at the restaurant door greet every guest with a wish for prosperity.

ctx.s: 新春贺卡上，他写了一句“{恭喜发财}，身体健康”。
ctx.en: On the New Year card he wrote: "Wishing you prosperity and good health."

bad.s: 他去年开公司赚了很多钱，真是{恭喜发财}了。
bad.en: (meant: he really got rich running his company last year)
bad.why: It is a greeting said to someone, not a description of a person getting rich.

bad.s: 朋友考上了大学，我对他说：“{恭喜发财}！”
bad.en: (meant: congratulations on getting into university)
bad.why: It wishes wealth, mainly at New Year; congratulating someone on an achievement calls for a plain 'congratulations'.

mean: may whatever you set your heart on come true
lit: what the heart thinks of, the matter is accomplished

use.how: Mostly after 祝你 or 愿你 in greetings and cards: 祝你生日快乐，心想事成！ Sometimes as an attributive: 心想事成的事.

near.diff: 万事如意 wishes that everything in general goes well; 心想事成 wishes that the things you are hoping for come true.

cue: A friend is about to apply for her dream job, and in her card you write that you hope what she is hoping for will happen. What do you wish her?

ctx.s: 快许个愿吧，祝你{心想事成}！
ctx.en: Go on, make a wish, and may it come true!

ctx.s: 他一直想开一家自己的咖啡馆，新年时我祝他{心想事成}。
ctx.en: He has always wanted to open a café of his own, so at New Year I wished that his dream would come true.

ctx.s: 他吹蜡烛前闭眼许愿，朋友们一起喊：“祝你{心想事成}！”
ctx.en: He closed his eyes to make a wish before blowing out the candles, and his friends shouted together: "May it come true!"

ctx.s: 听说你明年要考研究生，祝你{心想事成}，考上理想的学校。
ctx.en: I hear you're sitting the graduate entrance exam next year; I hope it all works out and you get into the school you want.

ctx.s: 同学知道我想当医生，在毕业纪念册上写：“愿你{心想事成}。”
ctx.en: Knowing I want to become a doctor, a classmate wrote in my yearbook: "May your dream come true."

ctx.s: 愿望归愿望，生活里哪有那么多{心想事成}的事呢？
ctx.en: Wishes are one thing, but how often in life do things turn out exactly as you hoped?

bad.s: 我{心想事成}这个周末去爬山。
bad.en: (meant: I'm thinking of going hiking this weekend)
bad.why: It is not a verb for planning or intending; it wishes that someone's hopes come true.

bad.s: 他遇到难题总是{心想事成}，一个问题能想一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he always thinks hard about difficult problems)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with thinking hard; it is about wishes being fulfilled.

mean: giving one's heart and strength to a task
lit: to use up all one's heart and all one's strength

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 她尽心尽力地照顾病人。 Said of devotion to a duty or to helping others; also as a promise: 我一定尽心尽力。

near.diff: 全力以赴 is throwing everything into one challenge or push; 尽心尽力 stresses conscientious, devoted care in a duty or in serving others.

cue: For years a nurse has cared for an elderly patient with total devotion, never cutting a corner. How do her colleagues describe the way she does her job?

ctx.s: 王老师对每个学生都{尽心尽力}。
ctx.en: Mr Wang gives his all to every one of his students.

ctx.s: 这些年她照顾生病的母亲，可以说是{尽心尽力}了。
ctx.en: In all these years of looking after her sick mother, she has truly done everything she could.

ctx.s: “我出差这段时间，我妈就拜托你照顾了。”“放心，我一定{尽心尽力}。”
ctx.en: "While I'm away on business, can I leave my mum in your care?" "Don't worry, I'll do everything I can for her."

ctx.s: 虽然最后没能救回病人，但医生们已经{尽心尽力}了。
ctx.en: Although in the end the patient could not be saved, the doctors had done everything they could.

ctx.s: 老张在这个小区当了十年物业经理，大家都说他办事{尽心尽力}。
ctx.en: Lao Zhang has managed this housing estate for ten years, and everyone says he is utterly conscientious.

ctx.s: 为了帮新同事熟悉工作，他{尽心尽力}，从不嫌麻烦。
ctx.en: He did everything he could to help the new colleague settle in, and never found it a bother.

bad.s: 放假了，我昨天{尽心尽力}地睡了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: I slept the whole day yesterday)
bad.why: It describes devoted effort for a duty or for other people, not doing a leisure activity a lot.

bad.s: 这道菜{尽心尽力}，非常好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this dish was made with great care and is delicious)
bad.why: It describes a person's effort, not a thing; say instead that the cook made it with great care.

mean: without a pause, moving straight on
lit: the horse does not stop its hooves

use.how: Adverbial, usually with 地 before a verb: 他下了飞机就马不停蹄地赶到会场。 Said of people going from one task or place straight on to the next.

near.diff: 争分夺秒 is racing against a deadline, using every minute; 马不停蹄 is going straight on from one task or place to the next without rest.

cue: Straight after landing, the manager goes to a meeting, then to a factory visit, then to a dinner, without even dropping her bags at the hotel. How did she move through the day?

ctx.s: 他下了飞机，{马不停蹄}地赶到了公司。
ctx.en: As soon as he got off the plane, he rushed straight to the office.

ctx.s: 这几天我{马不停蹄}，开完一个会又是另一个会。
ctx.en: These past few days I haven't stopped: one meeting ends and the next begins.

ctx.s: “你刚出差回来，不休息一下吗？”“没时间，明天还得{马不停蹄}地赶去上海。”
ctx.en: "You've only just got back from your trip; won't you rest?" "No time, tomorrow I have to head straight off to Shanghai."

ctx.s: 项目一结束，团队又{马不停蹄}地投入了下一个项目。
ctx.en: The moment the project finished, the team threw themselves straight into the next one.

ctx.s: 记者们{马不停蹄}地从一个现场跑到另一个现场。
ctx.en: The reporters dashed from one scene to the next without a break.

ctx.s: 救援队员三天三夜{马不停蹄}，挨家挨户地搜救。
ctx.en: For three days and nights the rescuers kept going without rest, searching house by house.

bad.s: 他做事总是{马不停蹄}，一点也不认真。
bad.en: (meant: he always does things hastily and carelessly)
bad.why: It means pressing on without rest and carries no criticism of careless, sloppy work.

bad.s: 雨{马不停蹄}地下了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: it rained nonstop all day)
bad.why: It is said of people pressing on from one task or place to the next, not of rain or weather that simply continues.

lit: to be counted first or second

use.how: Attributive with 的 or predicate, often with 在……里: 他的厨艺在我们这儿是数一数二的。 Says someone or something is among the best of a group or place.

near.diff: 名列前茅 is ranking near the top of a list, typically exam or contest results; 数一数二 says someone or something is among the very best of a field or place.

cue: Asked about a local chef, people say that in the whole city maybe one other cook could match him. Where does he stand?

ctx.s: 这家饭馆在我们城市是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: This restaurant is one of the very best in our city.

ctx.s: 他的篮球水平在全校{数一数二}。
ctx.en: At basketball he is one of the top players in the whole school.

ctx.s: “这家公司怎么样？”“在行业里算得上{数一数二}的大企业。”
ctx.en: "What's this company like?" "It's one of the leading firms in the industry."

ctx.s: 说到做菜，我妈在亲戚里可是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: When it comes to cooking, my mum is about the best among all our relatives.

ctx.s: 这座图书馆的藏书量在全国也是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: This library's collection is one of the largest in the whole country.

ctx.s: 他从一个普通工人，做到了公司里{数一数二}的技术专家。
ctx.en: He started as an ordinary worker and became one of the company's top technical experts.

bad.s: 我{数一数二}地把钱点了一遍。
bad.en: (meant: I counted the money one note at a time)
bad.why: It does not mean counting; it says something ranks among the best.

bad.s: 他{数一数二}了这次比赛。
bad.en: (meant: he took first or second place in the contest)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it describes a person or thing as ranking among the best.

mean: may you succeed straight away (a wish)
lit: success as soon as the horse arrives

use.how: Said as a wish before a contest, exam or venture: 祝你马到成功！ In formal send-offs: 预祝……马到成功。

near.diff: 一帆风顺 wishes a smooth journey or a smooth life; 马到成功 wishes quick success in a particular task someone is about to take on.

cue: Your friend is setting off this afternoon to pitch a deal to a big client. As they leave, what do you wish them?

ctx.s: 明天就要比赛了，祝你{马到成功}！
ctx.en: The competition is tomorrow; I hope you win it!

ctx.s: “我下午去面试。”“加油，祝你{马到成功}！”
ctx.en: "I've got an interview this afternoon." "Go for it, I hope you nail it!"

ctx.s: 考试前一天，妈妈给她发消息：“别紧张，祝你{马到成功}。”
ctx.en: The day before the exam her mother messaged her: "Don't be nervous, I know you'll pass with flying colours."

ctx.s: 出发前，同事们为谈判团队送行，预祝他们{马到成功}。
ctx.en: Before they set off, colleagues saw the negotiating team out and wished them quick success.

ctx.s: 他带队去参加全国大赛，校长握着他的手说：“祝你们{马到成功}！”
ctx.en: As he led the team off to the national contest, the headmaster shook his hand and said: "Go and win!"

ctx.s: 这次创业，朋友们都祝他{马到成功}，可他自己心里一点底也没有。
ctx.en: Friends all wished him instant success with his new business, but he himself had no idea how it would go.

bad.s: 爷爷今天退休了，我们祝他{马到成功}！
bad.en: (meant: we wished grandpa well in his retirement)
bad.why: It wishes quick success in a task about to begin; retirement is not a challenge to win.

bad.s: 他骑马骑得很好，每次都{马到成功}。
bad.en: (meant: he rides very well and always gets there)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with real horses; it is a wish for success in a venture.

mean: many small amounts add up to a lot
lit: pile up little and it becomes much

use.how: Usually a clause on its own after a small regular action: 每天存一点，积少成多。 Used to encourage saving or steady practice, or to warn that small things add up.

near.diff: 日积月累 stresses a long stretch of time; 积少成多 stresses that small amounts add up to a large one.

cue: Your friend says setting aside a few coins a day is pointless. You reply that those coins will eventually make a decent sum. What principle are you citing?

ctx.s: 每天存十块钱，{积少成多}，一年下来也不少。
ctx.en: Save ten yuan a day; it adds up, and by the end of the year it's quite a lot.

ctx.s: 一天背五个单词好像不多，但{积少成多}，一年就是一千八百多个。
ctx.en: Five words a day doesn't seem like much, but it adds up: in a year that's over eighteen hundred.

ctx.s: 别小看这些零钱，{积少成多}，够买一台电脑了。
ctx.en: Don't look down on this small change; it has added up to enough for a computer.

ctx.s: 奶奶把用过的塑料瓶攒起来卖，她说：“{积少成多}，能补贴点家用。”
ctx.en: Grandma saves used plastic bottles to sell. "Little by little it adds up," she says, "it helps with the household money."

ctx.s: 网上每人捐一块钱，{积少成多}，很快就筹够了手术费。
ctx.en: Online everyone gave one yuan, and together it soon covered the cost of the operation.

ctx.s: 小毛病如果不改，{积少成多}，最后会变成大问题。
ctx.en: If you don't fix small faults, they pile up and in the end become a big problem.

bad.s: 他买彩票一下子就{积少成多}，中了五百万。
bad.en: (meant: he suddenly got rich by winning five million in the lottery)
bad.why: It describes small amounts building up gradually, not a sudden windfall.

bad.s: 我想{积少成多}一笔钱去旅行。
bad.en: (meant: I want to save up a sum of money to travel)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; it comments on small amounts adding up, not on the act of saving.

lit: to memorise rigidly and recite by force

use.how: Predicate or attributive, mostly critical: 学语言不能只靠死记硬背。 Said of memorising study material without understanding it.

cue: A student can recite the whole textbook word for word but cannot answer a single question that asks him to explain it. How has he been studying?

ctx.s: 学数学不能{死记硬背}，要理解公式。
ctx.en: You can't learn maths by rote; you have to understand the formulas.

ctx.s: 考试前一晚，他把答案{死记硬背}了下来，第二天全忘了。
ctx.en: The night before the exam he crammed the answers by heart, and the next day he had forgotten them all.

ctx.s: “这些历史年代怎么记？”“别{死记硬背}，把事件串成故事就好记了。”
ctx.en: "How do I remember all these historical dates?" "Don't just drill them; link the events into a story and they'll stick."

ctx.s: 这种{死记硬背}的教学方法，早就该改一改了。
ctx.en: This rote-learning style of teaching should have been changed long ago.

ctx.s: 她小时候{死记硬背}过很多古诗，现在才慢慢懂得其中的意思。
ctx.en: As a child she learned lots of classical poems by rote, and only now is she slowly understanding them.

ctx.s: 面试官一听就知道，他的回答是{死记硬背}出来的。
ctx.en: The interviewer could tell at once that his answers had been memorised parrot-fashion.

bad.s: 他学习非常认真，每天都{死记硬背}，老师很表扬他。
bad.en: (meant: he studies very hard every day and the teacher praises him for it)
bad.why: It criticises memorising without understanding; it is not praise for diligence.

bad.s: 这本书的内容很{死记硬背}。
bad.en: (meant: this book's content is hard to memorise)
bad.why: It describes a way of learning, not a quality of the material being learned.

mean: to look around in all directions
lit: to look east and gaze west

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他站在门口东张西望。 Describes someone glancing this way and that, out of curiosity, while searching, or when they should be paying attention.

near.diff: 鬼鬼祟祟 says someone is acting furtively, hiding their purpose; 东张西望 only says they keep looking around.

cue: At a crowded station exit, a woman keeps turning her head this way and that, trying to spot the friend who is meant to pick her up. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 第一次进城，他好奇地{东张西望}。
ctx.en: On his first trip to the city, he looked all around him in curiosity.

ctx.s: 上课的时候别{东张西望}，认真听讲！
ctx.en: Don't keep looking around in class; listen properly!

ctx.s: 她站在车站出口{东张西望}，好像在等什么人。
ctx.en: She stood at the station exit looking this way and that, as if waiting for someone.

ctx.s: “你在找什么？”“我的钥匙不知道掉哪儿了。”他一边说一边{东张西望}。
ctx.en: "What are you looking for?" "I've dropped my keys somewhere," he said, glancing all around.

ctx.s: 小狗走丢以后，站在街口{东张西望}，不知道该往哪儿走。
ctx.en: After getting lost, the puppy stood at the corner looking every which way, not knowing where to go.

ctx.s: 考场上{东张西望}，很容易被当成作弊。
ctx.en: Looking around during an exam can easily get you taken for a cheat.

bad.s: 他{东张西望}了很久，最后决定去北京工作。
bad.en: (meant: he thought it over for a long time and decided to work in Beijing)
bad.why: It is physically looking around, not weighing a decision in one's mind.

bad.s: 他{东张西望}地盯着电脑屏幕工作了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: he stared at his screen working all afternoon)
bad.why: It means glancing restlessly in all directions, the opposite of keeping one's eyes fixed on one thing.

mean: to turn something over and over in one's mind
lit: to ponder on the left and think on the right

use.how: Predicate, usually followed by the outcome: 我左思右想，还是决定不去了。 Describes thinking a problem over from every side.

near.diff: 犹豫不决 is being stuck, unable to decide; 左思右想 is the act of thinking it over, which often ends in a decision or an idea.

cue: For two nights you go over every reason for and against moving to another city for a job, and in the end you say yes. What were you doing those two nights?

ctx.s: 我{左思右想}，还是决定不去了。
ctx.en: I thought it over and over, and decided not to go after all.

ctx.s: 他{左思右想}，觉得这件事还是先不告诉父母为好。
ctx.en: After turning it over and over, he felt it was better not to tell his parents just yet.

ctx.s: 晚上躺在床上，她{左思右想}，怎么也睡不着。
ctx.en: Lying in bed at night, she kept turning things over in her mind and couldn't get to sleep.

ctx.s: “你怎么才回消息？”“我{左思右想}，不知道该怎么回答你。”
ctx.en: "Why did it take you so long to reply?" "I kept going back and forth over it; I didn't know how to answer you."

ctx.s: 给女朋友挑生日礼物，他{左思右想}了好几天，最后选了一条围巾。
ctx.en: He agonised for days over a birthday present for his girlfriend and finally chose a scarf.

ctx.s: 经理{左思右想}，终于明白了问题出在哪里。
ctx.en: After thinking it through from every angle, the manager finally understood where the problem lay.

bad.s: 过马路的时候要{左思右想}，看看有没有车。
bad.en: (meant: look left and right for cars when crossing the road)
bad.why: It is about thinking, not physically looking left and right for traffic.

bad.s: 他是一个很{左思右想}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very thoughtful person)
bad.why: It describes mulling over one particular matter, not a personality trait, and cannot be modified by 'very'.
